summary: Fresh vision review of the b25-v4-pass-31 contact sheets fails B25. The screens have more domain-specific copy and actions than early harnesses, but the visible product still relies on a repeated stacked-card scaffold, weak visual identity, utility/evidence-like panels, and several dimmed action states. This does not yet feel like a modern production app across the reviewed communities/personas.

holisticQuestionAnswers.question: Does the whole experience feel like a real production community app for the target users, not merely an implemented workflow harness?
visibleEvidence: All eight contact sheets show many communities implemented through the same top app bar and stacked rounded-card pattern; domain nouns are present, but the screens still read as workflow-card variants.
holisticQuestionAnswers.requiredFix: Create differentiated community/product surfaces rather than relying on one universal card shell.

holisticQuestionAnswers.question: Is the UI modern, easy to use, easy to navigate, and visually appealing for the target persona?
visibleEvidence: The screens are cleaner than raw harness cards and use semantic actions, but the contact sheets show low component variety, repeated dense cards, limited hierarchy, and many dimmed action states.
holisticQuestionAnswers.requiredFix: Improve hierarchy, component variety, navigation affordances, and action-state clarity across the full pass.

holisticQuestionAnswers.question: Is the overall information architecture organized around community content and real jobs-to-be-done instead of workflow lists or validation surfaces?
visibleEvidence: Garden, book, mosque, soccer, HOA, and camera content is visible, but data portability, ad-off, platform social, export, and chess rows still foreground steps, state summaries, and evidence-style cards.
holisticQuestionAnswers.requiredFix: Reframe utility and platform flows as product IA: wizards, inbox/feed, billing settings, board/match views, and data previews.

holisticQuestionAnswers.question: Does the visible UI avoid blocking or major overlap, clipping, crowding, default-scaffold, repeated-card, checklist-modal, and thin-content defects?
visibleEvidence: Repeated-card fatigue is app-wide, and many action-state screenshots show low-contrast dimmed underlying content that makes the current task hard to scan.
holisticQuestionAnswers.requiredFix: Remove repeated-card dependence and replace dimmed action states with clear accessible production pages or modals.

findings.title: Primary experience still relies on one repeated stacked-card scaffold
visibleEvidence: Across contact sheets 001-195, Garden Club, Neighborhood Book Club, Riverside Youth Soccer, Cedar Commons HOA, Masjid Nur, Camera Club, Chess Club, Data Portability Community, Member Social Space, and Ad-Free Community all use the same narrow top app bar plus stacked rounded cards.
Repeated cards expose similar structures such as Event details, Payment summary, Submitted details, Export steps, Conversation, Package progress, and Request queue regardless of the community domain.

The domain copy is stronger than a harness, but the visible product still feels like workflow cards with improved nouns rather than differentiated event, feed, inbox, roster, document, billing, or export product surfaces.
concreteRequiredFixes: Redesign each primary workflow around a distinct domain-native surface instead of the universal card stack: event details with calendar/attendee affordances, book ballots with ranked choices and book metadata, soccer roster/schedule tables, HOA document and request queues, mosque announcement and care feeds, camera photo thumbnails, chess board or match-history views, export wizard tables, social inbox/feed surfaces, and billing/account settings.

Introduce screen-level information architecture with persistent section navigation, richer summaries, grouped controls, and task-specific layouts so users can distinguish communities and workflows at a glance.
Limit cards to actual repeated items or framed tools; do not make every screen a set of identical rounded panels with badges.
findings.requiredFix: Replace the repeated stacked-card shell with differentiated product surfaces for each community and workflow, then recapture B25 screenshots and rerun the LLM vision review.
acceptanceChecks: A contact sheet scan should show visibly different layouts for event RSVP, voting, payment, roster, document, announcement, social, export, ad-off, and chess workflows.
Primary workflow screenshots must not all share the same top-bar plus two-to-four rounded-card composition.
Every affected row needs fresh screenshots proving domain-specific content, actions, and hierarchy.

findings.title: Utility, export, ad, platform, and chess screens read as evidence/checklist panels rather than production products
visibleEvidence: Export and data portability screens repeatedly show Export steps, Package progress, Audit trail, Checksum evidence record, Provider transfer verification, and rollback cards instead of a wizard with tables, previews, redaction grids, and file actions.

Ad-Free Community and Member Social Space screens show Ad slot state, Ad-free account, Conversation, and Sponsored stream message panels that look like policy/evidence summaries more than account, billing, ad-placement, inbox, or feed product UI.
Chess Club rows show Club board and Board 1 match result as cards without a visible chess board, pairing table, standings, move history, or match-result UI depth.
concreteRequiredFixes: Build export/import as a real multi-step wizard with step navigation, dataset tables, row counts, conflict resolution, redaction field grids, checksum/file evidence, retry/rollback controls, and final downloadable artifacts.
Build ad-off as account/billing settings with plan status, member/community scope, amount, payment method, receipt history, entitlement, and clear restore/manage actions.
Build platform social as an inbox/feed with thread list, participants, message composer, connection state, safety state, and sponsored placement disclosure in the feed context.
Build Chess Club around a board/match product surface with board visualization, round, players, result entry, standings or match history, and clear save/record result states.
findings.requiredFix: Convert utility-looking evidence panels into full product flows with concrete records, tables, previews, and task-specific controls before B25 can pass.
acceptanceChecks: Data/export rows show actual wizard navigation and data previews rather than only an ordered checklist.
Ad-off rows show billing/account surfaces rather than generic account cards.
Platform rows show an inbox/feed/thread experience with message composition and state.
Chess rows show chess-specific board or match structures rather than generic cards.

findings.title: Many action and decision states are dimmed or visually occluded instead of clear production interaction states
visibleEvidence: Several middle/action-state screenshots show a dark overlay or underlay with text still visible behind the foreground card, making the decision state feel like a test overlay rather than a shippable screen.

Examples across book voting, search answers, soccer redaction/export, HOA requests/notices, mosque receipt/care, platform messages, ad-off controls, and export workflows show low-contrast background content and partially obscured sections.
Because the action state is visually dimmed, the user cannot reliably scan the current decision, alternate action, confirmation, or result as a normal production page.
concreteRequiredFixes: Use full-height action/review/result pages or properly constrained accessible modals; avoid dimming large prior-screen content unless it is a real modal with one clear focus and high-contrast foreground controls.

Ensure every action state has readable contrast, visible title, current object, decision information, primary action, change/reject/defer path, and persistent result state without relying on obscured background text.
Recapture action-state screenshots after fixing contrast and state presentation.
findings.requiredFix: Redesign action, decision, review, and confirmation states so they are clear production interaction surfaces, not dimmed evidence overlays.
acceptanceChecks: Foreground and background text meet contrast expectations and no critical content is hidden behind translucent overlays.
The action state can be understood from the screenshot without reading the previous card behind it.
Each affected workflow shows a clear persistent result or receipt after the action.

findings.title: Community identity and visual differentiation remain too weak for a modern production app
visibleEvidence: Most screens rely on a solid color family, small line icons, chips, and text cards. There are no visible garden photos, book covers, soccer roster affordances, HOA document previews, mosque/community imagery, camera thumbnails, chess boards, data-table previews, or account/billing visuals at production depth.

The communities are color-coded, but the contact sheets still read as variations of the same template rather than distinct Garden Club, Masjid Nur, HOA, soccer, camera, chess, social, ad-free, and data portability products.
The bottom contact-sheet labels are not app UI, but the app screenshots themselves show limited visual hierarchy and a narrow component vocabulary.
concreteRequiredFixes: Add community-specific identity treatments and domain-native visual elements: garden plant cards/photos, book cover/ballot treatment, soccer schedule/roster tables, HOA document thumbnails/status queue, mosque announcement/feed styling, camera image thumbnails, chess board/match widgets, data grids, and billing/account panels.
Use typographic hierarchy, section layouts, empty/result states, and component variety so the screen communicates the product category before the user reads every badge.
Keep palettes accessible and differentiated; avoid letting green/blue/purple/brown skins be the only distinction between communities.
findings.requiredFix: Raise visual identity and product-surface depth across all communities before another B25 review.
acceptanceChecks: A reviewer can identify each community/workflow category visually without relying only on the app-bar title.
Primary screens contain at least one domain-specific visual or structural component appropriate to the task.
Screens show stronger hierarchy and less card-only composition across desktop-sized contact sheets and phone screenshots.
